name: Jacob Malkoun
summary: Whittaker training partner and 31-year-old Australian middleweight (10-3; 6-3 in the UFC) on a three-fight win streak. A pressure wrestler who has added real striking since his long injury layoff, battering Torrez Finney (117 significant strikes, a knockdown) before edging Gerald Meerschaert on his jab. Seven of his ten wins are three-round decisions.

how_they_fight.Striking: Much improved: about 5 significant strikes a minute at 52% with 64% defense. Against Meerschaert he walked him to the fence behind a steady jab; against Finney he dropped him twice per Cageside Press (one knockdown in our stats) and won every round. Finished Andre Petroski with strikes 39 seconds into round two.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Chain wrestler with a high-volume shot (3.6 takedowns per 15, 39% accuracy): 8 of 24 vs Abdul Razak Alhassan with almost 12 minutes of control, 9 of 13 vs Nick Maximov, 7 of 14 vs Brendan Allen. Not a submission threat himself, and his grappling can backfire: Meerschaert reversed his first-round shot and rode him, then had a guillotine late in round three.
how_they_fight.Defense: Durable since the debut: stopped once, by Phil Hawes in 18 seconds in 2020. About 69% takedown defense; Allen out-grappled him in a close decision loss in 2022.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Three-round grinder who keeps the same pace for 15 minutes; he has gone the distance in 7 of 10 wins plus the Allen loss. Finishes are rare and scattered (regional R1 and R3 KOs, Petroski early R2). Losses: R1 KO (Hawes), R1 DQ (Brundage), R3 decision (Allen). Opponents describe his stamina as a strength; Vagaev said he has seen Malkoun 'go all the way' with a steady pace.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Mostly sound and adaptable: after losing round one on control to Meerschaert, he kept the fight standing in round two. Discipline lapse on record: the 2023 loss to Cody Brundage was a first-round disqualification, which Heavy ties to an illegal elbow.

patterns: Goes to decision: 7 of 10 wins and 6 of 9 UFC fights
Wins later rounds with volume and pressure rather than early finishes
Mixes jab-led pressure with repeated takedown attempts
Bounced back from layoffs and losses with three straight wins (Petroski, Finney, Meerschaert)
concerns: Size: a compact middleweight (175 cm) facing a 183 cm opponent moving up from welterweight
Strong grapplers can reverse or ride him (Allen, Meerschaert round one)
Was stopped in 18 seconds in his debut; early chaos is his only stoppage risk on record
Injury-prone stretch: about 22 months out between March 2024 and January 2026, with cancelled fights he acknowledged per Cageside Press
Fighting in Abu Dhabi, far from his Australian base, on his third UFC card of 2026
keys_to_beat: Defend his early shots and make him pay for level changes
Get top position in scrambles; he does not threaten much off his back
Hurt him early before his volume takes over
Match his pace with clinch control to steal rounds

news.text: Booked vs Abubakar Vagaev at middleweight for UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi, his third UFC appearance of 2026; aiming for a fourth straight win.
Beat Gerald Meerschaert 29-28 x3 at UFC Perth after losing round one on control and surviving a late guillotine.
Returned from a long injury layoff to beat unbeaten Torrez Finney 30-27, 30-26, 30-26 at UFC 325; Finney later said he tore his ACL and menisci 15 seconds in.
Record note: Heavy (via Yahoo) lists the 2023 Cody Brundage fight as a Malkoun win by disqualification; our verified data has Brundage winning by DQ in R1 (4:15), so Malkoun is 10-3, not 11-2.
